exampleAnswers.title: Estimating a Mean From Grouped Data

question.text:
A restaurant manager records the total time $20$ customers waited before they were seated. The results are presented in the table below.


Waiting time (minutes) Frequency
$0 \leq x \lt 10$ $4$
$10 \leq x \lt 15$ $6$
$15\leq x \lt 20$ $7$
$20\leq x \lt 30$ $3$
\[\]

Assuming that the waiting times within each class interval are uniformly distributed, find an estimate of the mean waiting time $\overline x,$ rounded to one decimal place.
question.explanation:
Given a frequency table containing continuous data split into $K$ classes, the mean can be estimated as follows: \[ \overline x \approx \dfrac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^K f_i \cdot m_{i} \] where

  • $f_i$ is the frequency of the $i$th class,

  • $m_i$ is the midpoint of the $i$th class, and

  • $n$ is the total number of observations.

To estimate the mean, we add columns to our table for the midpoints of each class and the products of the midpoints and frequencies.

Waiting time (minutes) $f_i$ $m_i$ $f_i \cdot m_i$
$0 \leq x \lt 10$ $4$ $5$ $20$
$10 \leq x \lt 15$ $6$ $12.5$ $75$
$15 \leq x \lt 20$ $7$ $17.5$ $122.5$
$20 \leq x \lt 30$ $3$ $25$ $75$
\[\]

Finally, we sum the values in the last column and divide by $20$ (the total number of observations). \begin{align*} \overline x &\approx \dfrac{20+75+122.5+75}{20} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{292.5}{20} \\[5pt] &\approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{14.6} \end{align*}

question.text: An experiment consists of taking $14$ measurements of rainfall (in $\textrm{mm}$) during the rainy season in Africa. The results are presented above in the form of a histogram. Assuming that the rainfall measurements within each class interval are uniformly distributed, find an estimate of the mean rainfall, rounded to two decimal places.
question.explanation:
Given a frequency table containing continuous data split into $K$ classes, the mean can be estimated as follows: \[ \overline x \approx \dfrac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^K f_i \cdot m_{i} \] where

  • $f_i$ is the frequency of the $i$th class,

  • $m_i$ is the midpoint of the $i$th class, and

  • $n$ is the total number of observations.

To estimate the mean, we represent the given data as a table and add columns for the midpoints of each class and the products of the midpoints and frequencies.

Rainfall ($\textrm{mm}$) $m_i$ $f_i$ $m_i \cdot f_i$
$200 \leq r \lt 250$ $225$ $3$ $675$
$250 \leq r \lt 300$ $275$ $5$ $1375$
$300 \leq r \lt 350$ $325$ $4$ $1300$
$350 \leq r \lt 400$ $375$ $2$ $750$
\[\]

Finally, we sum the values in the last column and divide by $14$ (the total number of observations).

\begin{align*} \overline r &\approx \dfrac{675+1375+1300+750}{14} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{4100}{14} \\[5pt] & \approx 292.86\,\textrm{mm} \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Estimating a Variance or Standard Deviation

question.text:
Consider the frequency table below for a continuous variable $x.$ The total number of observations is $n = 15,$ and the estimated sample mean is $\overline x \approx 23.$


Range Frequency $(f_i)$
$0\leq x \lt 10$ $2$
$10 \leq x \lt 20$ $4$
$20\leq x \lt 30$ $4$
$30\leq x \lt 40$ $5$
\[ \]

Using the midpoint of each class interval to approximate all observations within that class, estimate the standard deviation $\sigma_n,$ using $n$ as the denominator in the variance formula.
question.explanation:
Given a frequency table containing continuous data split into $K$ classes, we can estimate the variance by treating all observations within each class as though they were equal to the midpoint of that class. This gives \[ \sigma^2_n \approx \dfrac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^K f_i \cdot (m_{i} - \overline x)^2, \] where

  • $f_i$ is the frequency of the $i$th class,

  • $m_i$ is the midpoint of the $i$th class,

  • $n$ is the total number of observations, and

  • $\overline x$ is the estimated mean, calculated using the class midpoints.

To find the variance, we add columns to our table for the midpoints of each interval, the squared deviations of the midpoints from the mean, and the products of the squared deviations and frequencies.



Range $f_i$ $m_i$ $\left(m_i - \overline x\right)^2 $ $f_i \left(m_i - \overline x\right)^2$
$0 \leq x \lt 10$ $2$ $5$ $324$ $648$
$10 \leq x \lt 20$ $4$ $15$ $64$ $256$
$20\leq x \lt 30$ $4$ $25$ $4$ $16$
$30\leq x \lt 40$ $5$ $35$ $144$ $720$
\[\]

Then, we divide the sum of all the values in the last column by $15$ (the total number of observations): \begin{align*} \sigma^2_n &\approx \dfrac{648+256+16+720}{15}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1640}{15} \\[5pt] & \approx 109.3333 \end{align*}

Finally, the estimated standard deviation is the square root of the estimated variance: \begin{align*} \sigma_n &\approx \sqrt{109.3333} \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{10.5} \end{align*}

example.title: Estimating a Variance or Standard Deviation

question.text:
A teacher wants to estimate the standard deviation of some students' grades on the final math exam. The following frequency table records the students' grades.


Grades ($x_i$) Frequency $(f_i)$
$50 \leq x \lt 60$ $2$
$60 \leq x \lt 70$ $5$
$70 \leq x \lt 80$ $10$
$80\leq x \lt 90$ $6$
$90\leq x \lt 100$ $5$
\[\]

The estimated mean grade is $\overline x \approx 77.5.$ Using the midpoint of each class interval to approximate all observations within that class, estimate the standard deviation $\sigma_n,$ using $n$ as the denominator in the variance formula.
question.explanation:
Given a frequency table containing data split into $K$ classes, we can estimate the variance by treating all observations within each class as though they were equal to the midpoint of that class. This gives \[ \sigma^2_n \approx \dfrac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^K f_i \cdot (m_{i} - \overline x)^2, \] where

  • $f_i$ is the frequency of the $i$th class,

  • $m_i$ is the midpoint of the $i$th class,

  • $n$ is the total number of observations, and

  • $\overline x$ is the estimated mean, calculated using the class midpoints.

To find the variance, we add columns to our table for the midpoints of each interval, the squared deviations of the midpoints from the mean, and the products of the squared deviations and frequencies.



$x_i$ $f_i$ $m_i$ $\left(m_i - \overline x\right)^2 $ $f_i \left(m_i - \overline x\right)^2$
$50 \leq x \lt 60$ $2$ $55$ $506.25$ $1012.5$
$60 \leq x \lt 70$ $5$ $65$ $156.25$ $781.25$
$70\leq x \lt 80$ $10$ $75$ $6.25$ $62.5$
$80\leq x \lt 90$ $6$ $85$ $56.25$ $337.5$
$90\leq x \lt 100$ $5$ $95$ $306.25$ $1531.25$
\[\]

Then, we divide the sum of all the values in the last column by the total number of observations: \begin{align*} \sigma^2_n &\approx \dfrac{1012.5 + 781.25 + 62.5 + 337.5 + 1531.25}{2+5+10+6+5}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{3725}{28} \\[5pt] & \approx 133.0357 \end{align*}

Finally, the estimated standard deviation is the square root of the estimated variance: \begin{align*} \sigma_n &\approx \sqrt{133.0357} \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{11.5} \end{align*}
